reasoning: Per-share basis: every per-share figure (target, EPS, scenarios, ladder, thesis break) is per CURRENT pre-split share, i.e. today's Class A share plus the Class C share it receives on 2027-01-19; EV is unchanged. Facts: Q3-26 revenue $64.6B (+26%), impressions +10% (slowest in five quarters), price per ad +14%, a $9.89B AG settlement charge, FCF -$2.1B, capex guide $135-145B, Q4 guide $73-76B, RL loss ~$15B in 2027, Class C non-voting share for capital raising; the stock went 697.52 -> 642.62 (-8%) after the print. Alternative-data lane: Sensor Tower via TechCrunch/PPC Land shows Muse at #1 in US app stores, 10.9M downloads in 40 days and 2.5M US DAU, but D1->D14 retention decays ~50 points and Meta is steering 39% of its own ad spend to it; Polymarket prices Meta at 1.4% to hold the best model at end-2026 ($3.0M volume) - Meta is a fast follower, not the frontier leader; Similarweb has Threads ahead of X on mobile DAU; a 230-brand agency network (Common Thread) shows Meta ROAS down 39% since Feb-2024, the counterweight to +14% pricing; Trefis and Deep Research Global (Substack) flag that the summer +37% run was ad-machine driven and that 2027-28 margins are exposed to underutilised capex. Reddit and X were not reachable through search, so social sentiment is not used. Model: driver-led (impressions x price for 97.6% of revenue; FoA cash margin; RL loss; capex from the AI capex file base; D&A from a vintage model). FY2027 revenue $310.0B (consensus $311.3B, -0.4%); EBIT $102.2B (consensus-implied ~$104B); reported EPS $32.50 vs consensus $33.92 (-4%, because our D&A follows the higher AI-file capex). Guidance checked against the record: quarterly revenue beats narrowed to ~2-3%; expense guides land within ~1.5% of midpoint; capex first guides are pro-cyclical (+16-21% in build years). Valuation: P/E 18.5x core EPS ex RL ($695.57) and FoA 11.0x EBITDA SOTP ($724.93), RL valued once as a -$55B venture adjustment, litigation -$15.7B expected; research target (12m) $710.25 (+10.5%). Not driver-linked: none (both legs and the adjustments are computed from drivers or stated inputs). Distribution: engine scenarios bear $461 (25%) / base $710 (50%) / bull $926 (25%). Because today's price beats any blend as a forecast, our ladder centres the base at ~$685 (between price and target), with within-scenario sigmas 0.21-0.24, giving a median ~$677 and log-sd ~0.33 (below the 43% realized vol, in line with the 25-35% large-cap base rate after the post-earnings reset). P(>= $643) 56%, P(>= $771) 34%, P(< $450) 13%.

model_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led set: 6 drivers (impressions index, price-per-ad index, FoA cash margin, RL loss, capex, D&A) compute FoA ad revenue (97.6% of base revenue), FoA EBIT, RL EBIT, capex and D&A. Value carried by two legs at 50/50: P/E 18.5x on core GAAP EPS ex Reality Labs (driver-linked stated EPS) and a SOTP with Family of Apps at 11.0x NTM EBITDA (driver-linked). Reality Labs is valued once, as a -$55B equity adjustment (playbook: never run venture losses through the core multiple). Litigation in adjustments. No DCF leg (not a neocloud). Leg weights are judgment, untested.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) capex 2027-28 follows the AI capex file base ($192B/$236B) which is above Meta's 2027 consensus ($164-186B); D&A follows. (2) RL venture value -$55B vs running RL losses through the P/E (-$75/share more). (3) Shares held flat: GAAP EPS costs SBC and buybacks are paused (TTM 0, F67); possible Class C capital raises are not modelled as dilution because cash raised offsets them at fair value. (4) FY2026 tax 16% is used, not the 9M actual (Q1 had an $8.0B one-off benefit), so model FY2026 EPS is below consensus by design.
